unit.why: A halakhic-homiletic passage on tefillin that contains a short legend about a disciple of the Ari who appeared to him in a dream after death; it ends with a gematria explanation.
unit.boundary_note: the passage continues a sequence of tefillin teachings ('מענין תפילין') from the previous division

stories.start_quote: מעשה בתלמיד א׳ ותיק של הק׳ אר״י
stories.summary_en: A pious disciple of the Ari appears to him in a dream after his death. He reports that his state in the world to come is very good, but he was judged strictly for one thing: while concentrating intensely on 'ולמען לא ניגע לריק' in the Kedusha de-Sidra, he let his mind stray from his tefillin.

tags.why: Legend about the Ari and his circle, a pre-Hasidic kabbalist
The narrative sits inside a halakhic-homiletic frame with a gematria explanation
The dead disciple appears to the Ari in a dream
The Ari converses with the soul of the dead disciple
The disciple's death opens the story
Distraction from the tefillin is the sin he was judged for

tags.why: His intense mystical intention on a specific phrase of the prayer
